comparisons.peer_topic: Income Tax Provision and Effective Rate
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD recorded an income tax provision of $381 million in 2024 with a 19% effective tax rate, compared to a $346 million benefit and (68%) rate in 2023. The 2024 provision increase was driven by higher pre-tax income and a $373 million tax effect from an intercompany integration transaction.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD reported a 2024 effective tax rate below the U.S. statutory rate of 21%, driven by specific tax benefits, though the underlying drivers differed. NVDA’s 2024 rate was lowered by a benefit from an IRS audit resolution which partially offset decreases in benefits from FDII and stock-based compensation. AMD recorded a 19% effective tax rate in 2024, driven by higher pre-tax income and a $373 million tax effect from an intercompany integration transaction, contrasting with NVDA’s focus on audit resolution and FDII changes.

comparisons.peer_topic: Valuation allowance and effective tax rate change
comparisons.peer_summary: The effective tax rate increased in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily due to the establishment of a valuation allowance against US federal deferred tax assets in 2024. This allowance was recognized in the third quarter of 2024 after determining it was more likely than not that the assets would not be recoverable, largely due to a three-year cumulative historical loss position resulting from asset impairment and restructuring charges.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies discussed the drivers behind their 2024 effective tax rate movements, but the direction and causes were opposite. NVDA stated that its effective tax rate was lower than the statutory rate due to a benefit from an IRS audit resolution. In contrast, INTC reported that its effective tax rate increased in 2024 primarily due to the establishment of a valuation allowance against U.S. federal deferred tax assets, which negatively impacted the rate compared to prior years.
